Check: Define exactly what appears duplicated
Evidence to capture: Customer; site; hostnames; platform record URLs; first observed time; reporter
Likely cause: Two console objects; one endpoint changing identity; stale inventory; naming collision
Safe next action: Preserve both records and describe the visible conflict before changing either
Escalation trigger: The records belong to different customers or ownership is unclear

Check: Record authoritative platform and endpoint identifiers
Evidence to capture: Platform device IDs; agent IDs; enrollment IDs; tenant and site; endpoint serial; UUID; hostname
Likely cause: Hostname reused; record cloned; agent identity duplicated
Safe next action: Capture stable identifiers from both console and endpoint
Escalation trigger: Privileged records share an identity or identifiers disagree across tenants

Check: Build the change and activity timeline
Evidence to capture: Image date; install or reinstall time; reimage event; first and last heartbeat; job and user activity
Likely cause: Golden image; reimage; reinstall; restore; delayed import; stale record
Safe next action: Correlate the first identity conflict with a documented change
Escalation trigger: No authorized change explains the duplicate

Check: Set authority; stop conditions; and communication
Evidence to capture: System owner; customer approval; business impact; maintenance window; rollback; contact record
Likely cause: Uncoordinated cleanup could remove the active device or its history
Safe next action: Define who may retire; reset; merge; or re-enroll each record
Escalation trigger: Production-critical endpoint or customer ownership is disputed

Check: Capture local agent identity without modifying it
Evidence to capture: Agent ID; device key or certificate reference; enrollment metadata; install path; agent version
Likely cause: Cloned local identity; stale credential; reused enrollment package
Safe next action: Use read-only vendor-supported inspection methods
Escalation trigger: Identity material appears exposed; copied; or altered

Check: Capture durable hardware and operating-system identifiers
Evidence to capture: Serial number; hardware UUID; system drive ID if supported; OS install date; machine SID only when relevant
Likely cause: Cloned VM; restored snapshot; replacement board; reimage; shared hardware ID
Safe next action: Compare multiple durable identifiers; do not rely on hostname alone
Escalation trigger: Hardware identifiers collide unexpectedly across physical devices

Check: Capture network and naming context
Evidence to capture: Hostname; domain; IP; MAC addresses; adapter types; DHCP history; site; NAT or proxy context
Likely cause: Hostname reuse; virtual adapter cloning; MAC reuse; network inventory lag
Safe next action: Separate naming collisions from agent-identity collisions
Escalation trigger: MAC or hostname maps to another customer's endpoint

Check: Preserve platform history and audit evidence
Evidence to capture: Record creation time; tenant and site moves; last seen; inventory; scripts; patches; alerts; audit actors
Likely cause: Stale object; API import; manual move; duplicate enrollment
Safe next action: Export or screenshot the histories before retirement or merge
Escalation trigger: Audit history is missing; altered; or shows unexplained privileged actions

Check: Check whether an agent was captured in a golden image
Evidence to capture: Image build record; installed services; enrollment state at capture; deployment cohort
Likely cause: Agent installed or enrolled before image sealing
Safe next action: Stop further deployment and follow the vendor's image-preparation procedure
Escalation trigger: The same identity is spreading to additional endpoints

Check: Check reinstall; reimage; and restore behavior
Evidence to capture: Uninstall result; reinstall package; reimage or restore timestamp; prior record mapping
Likely cause: Old identity survived reinstall; a new record was created; snapshot restored stale state
Safe next action: Map old and new identities before choosing the authoritative record
Escalation trigger: Reinstall created cross-tenant placement or two active privileged records

Check: Check enrollment tokens; keys; certificates; and device IDs
Evidence to capture: Token source; certificate thumbprint; key age; device ID; rotation or revocation record
Likely cause: Shared token or identity material; revoked or reused enrollment credential
Safe next action: Use the vendor-supported identity reset or renewal workflow
Escalation trigger: Possible credential exposure or unauthorized reuse

Check: Check APIs; imports; integrations; and reconciliation jobs
Evidence to capture: API request IDs; connector logs; import source; CMDB IDs; retry history; webhook events
Likely cause: Duplicate create call; retry without idempotency; stale import; mapping bug
Safe next action: Disable only the failing writer and preserve request evidence
Escalation trigger: An integration is creating duplicates across customers or at fleet scale

Check: Pause automation on ambiguous records
Evidence to capture: Policies; scheduled scripts; patch jobs; alert actions; remote-session availability
Likely cause: Both records can execute privileged work against one endpoint
Safe next action: Suspend high-risk automation on the ambiguous objects only
Escalation trigger: Automation cannot be scoped without disrupting critical service

Check: Stop propagation from images or deployment tooling
Evidence to capture: Image version; task sequence; install package; deployment rule; affected cohort
Likely cause: Identity-bearing image or reusable package continues to clone records
Safe next action: Quarantine the source artifact and create a corrected pilot
Escalation trigger: New duplicates continue after the source is paused

Check: Protect tenant boundaries and customer ownership
Evidence to capture: Tenant; site; customer contract; endpoint owner; data visible in each record
Likely cause: Wrong-tenant enrollment; manual move; reused installer; integration mapping error
Safe next action: Disable access and automation until the correct tenant is proven
Escalation trigger: Any cross-customer visibility or control is confirmed

Check: Preserve ticket; alert; patch; and audit history
Evidence to capture: Linked tickets; alert history; patch state; scripts; notes; attachments; approvals
Likely cause: Deleting a stale record would destroy operational evidence
Safe next action: Export or link history before archive; merge; or retirement
Escalation trigger: Retention; legal; security; or customer evidence could be lost

Check: Choose the authoritative endpoint and platform record
Evidence to capture: Decision owner; durable identifiers; current heartbeat; user or workload; history value
Likely cause: No agreed source of truth; both records partially current
Safe next action: Document why one identity is authoritative and what will happen to the other
Escalation trigger: Authority cannot be proven or both records remain active

Check: Reset or re-enroll identity through the vendor-supported path
Evidence to capture: Approved procedure; backup; reset result; new agent ID; tenant and site placement
Likely cause: Cloned identity requires unique enrollment
Safe next action: Pilot the supported reset on one endpoint and verify placement
Escalation trigger: Procedure removes evidence; changes tenant; or fails to create a unique identity

Check: Archive; merge; or retire the non-authoritative record safely
Evidence to capture: Retirement reason; export; retained links; final status; approver; time
Likely cause: Stale or superseded platform object
Safe next action: Prefer archive or supported merge over destructive deletion
Escalation trigger: The platform offers only irreversible deletion or retention is required

Check: Repair downstream mappings and open work
Evidence to capture: CMDB ID; ticket links; billing; backup; EDR; PSA; documentation; integration keys
Likely cause: Downstream systems still reference the retired object
Safe next action: Update mappings and reconcile all open jobs and alerts
Escalation trigger: Billing; security; backup; or customer records remain attached to the wrong identity

Check: Prove each endpoint now has one unique active identity
Evidence to capture: Unique platform ID; unique local identity; current tenant and site; current heartbeat
Likely cause: Reset incomplete; stale record still active; identity collision persists
Safe next action: Wait the documented ingestion interval and compare both sides again
Escalation trigger: Two endpoints still report through one identity or one endpoint has two active records

Check: Test inventory; monitoring; jobs; patching; and remote access
Evidence to capture: Fresh inventory; alert test; bounded script; patch scan; remote-session audit
Likely cause: Partial reconciliation; downstream module still points to stale record
Safe next action: Test each privileged function separately and retain results
Escalation trigger: A privileged action runs against the wrong endpoint or lacks audit evidence

Check: Sweep the affected cohort for hidden duplicates
Evidence to capture: Image cohort; deployment wave; agent version; tenant; site; matching identifiers; exception list
Likely cause: The visible pair is part of a larger cloned or imported cohort
Safe next action: Run a read-only cohort reconciliation and assign every exception
Escalation trigger: Unknown; cross-tenant; or actively colliding records remain

Check: Update images; enrollment; integration; and reconciliation controls
Evidence to capture: Corrected image version; install timing; idempotency rule; duplicate alert; runbook; review date
Likely cause: Root process can recreate the identity conflict
Safe next action: Add pre-deployment identity checks and periodic duplicate detection
Escalation trigger: Prevention owner; test; or review date is missing
